name: Gmail
scenario: External server-based AI agent that reads and summarizes a user's Gmail messages using gmail.readonly; public SaaS distribution, not an internal-only Workspace tool.

verdict.headline: You can test before review. Public Gmail read access is a restricted-scope launch project.
verdict.reason: Reading mail requires a restricted scope. A server that can access restricted data ordinarily adds third-party security assessment and recurring compliance work.
verdict.nextAction: Confirm whether the agent truly needs mailbox reading, or whether send-only or user-triggered add-on access satisfies the feature.

time.testSetup: 45–90 minutes active effort (author estimate; assumes account/project access and a working OAuth backend).
time.productionPrep: 1–3 days active preparation (author estimate); engineering and CASA remediation can add substantially more.
time.reviewWait: Google FAQ baseline: restricted scopes about 6 weeks; sensitive scopes about 10 business days; branding about 2–3 business days. Estimates are not guaranteed and depend on responsiveness.
time.timingNuance: Current restricted-scope guide describes automated brand review finishing in minutes when checks pass, with manual review possible. Do not add the review stages into a guaranteed launch date.
time.assessmentCost: Assessment price and work were not verified; obtain an assessor quote before committing to launch.

scopeChoices.purpose: Read mailbox messages; matches this guide's scenario.
Headers/metadata only; reducing content does not remove restricted review.
Send-only feature may avoid restricted scopes, but cannot read or summarize messages.
Label management; cannot replace message-reading access.

testVsProduction.testing: Use External + Testing and explicitly add test accounts; Google documents a 100-user allowlist cap. Gmail-scope refresh tokens expire after 7 days in this state, so long-running tests must handle reconnects.
testVsProduction.production: Publishing alone is insufficient for public restricted-scope launch. Complete brand and scope verification, and the applicable security assessment.
testVsProduction.internalAlternative: An Internal app owned by a Workspace/Cloud Identity organization is a separate path for that organization's users only. It is not a shortcut for external customers.
testVsProduction.adminNuance: Workspace admins can block even verified apps; provider verification does not override customer admin controls.

steps.title: Establish the test project
steps.action: Select or create a dedicated non-production Cloud project with appropriate access; enable Gmail API. Use a separate production project for launch.
steps.doneWhen: Gmail API is enabled in the intended test project.

steps.title: Configure consent and audience
steps.action: Google Auth platform → Branding → Get Started. Set app name, support/contact emails and External audience. Review the policy yourself. In Audience add authorized test accounts.
steps.doneWhen: Branding is configured and your test account is allowlisted.

steps.title: Declare exactly the scopes the feature uses
steps.action: Data Access → Add or remove scopes. Select gmail.readonly only if the summarization feature needs it. Confirm its restricted classification.
steps.doneWhen: Declared scopes match the real authorization request.

steps.title: Create the server OAuth client
steps.action: Clients → Create Client → Web application. Add your integration runtime's exact callback in Authorized redirect URIs. Inspect the AI-powered agent option; use a separate client for mixed standard and agent workflows. Store returned confidential client configuration in your backend secret manager.
steps.doneWhen: The runtime has the intended client configuration and callback; secrets stay outside guides and source control.

steps.title: Connect one test user
steps.action: Run the authorization-code flow through your integration runtime; for background access request offline access, verify state and securely exchange/store tokens. Confirm a read succeeds with minimum data and reconnect works.
steps.doneWhen: A test user grants consent and a real Gmail read succeeds. This investigation did not execute that test.

steps.title: Prepare public-launch evidence
steps.owner: Agent drafts; developer records and reviews
steps.action: Prepare public homepage/privacy information, domain ownership, scope justification and a working reviewer demonstration. For automation platforms demonstrate workflows and data direction. Explain AI data processing and deletion.
steps.doneWhen: A reviewer can follow the user journey and see why each scope is needed.

steps.title: Submit and resolve review
steps.action: In production, publish verified branding before requesting data access review in Verification Center. If restricted data is accessible from/through servers, follow Google's approved-assessor process. Track requests in contact email and Verification Center.
steps.doneWhen: Required verification and assessment are approved, then production connection tests succeed. Neither approval nor this final test was attempted.

blockers.remedy: Confirm the selected Google account is in the External Testing allowlist. Check customer Workspace admin restrictions as a separate cause.
Copy the exact callback from the actual auth runtime and match scheme, host, port and path in the correct client's redirect list. Google notes settings can take 5 minutes to hours to propagate.
Check External + Testing token expiry before treating it as a refresh implementation defect. Reconnect for testing; complete the production path for launch.
Use Verification Center and Google's email request to identify the missing evidence. Fix the scoped issue and respond; avoid changing scopes mid-review without reassessing impact.

blockers.symptom: CASA budget or schedule blocks launch
blockers.remedy: Get an assessor quote and review data architecture. Reduce scopes only when the narrower feature actually satisfies user needs; never represent server-hosted processing as on-device.

canDo: Find official requirements and scope categories
Prepare a scope-to-feature justification and review checklist
Draft consent, policy and reviewer-demo materials for human review
Inspect accessible setup UI and identify exact human handoff
humanMustDo: Choose the production owner and app identity
Create credentials and keep them in a secure runtime
Grant test-account consent and approve access
Attest to privacy/data handling, submit review, and engage an assessor
notPossibleToGuarantee: Approval date or security assessment cost

setupAttempt.level: Live console form inspected; no app created
actions: Opened the live Clients console in a browser
Opened Create client and selected Web application
Read the creation fields and AI-agent help tooltip without entering identifiers, creating a client, or submitting changes
observed: Current navigation uses Branding, Audience, Clients, Data Access and Verification Center
Web form exposes Name, Authorized JavaScript origins, Authorized redirect URIs
Form exposes Use this client for an AI-powered agent
Tooltip recommends separate OAuth clients for AI-agent and standard features, and calls out Google MCP tools
Form warns settings may take 5 minutes to hours to take effect
setupAttempt.handoff: Stopped before Create; no credentials generated, copied, submitted or stored. Existing project/account details are intentionally excluded from this shareable dossier.

learnedAndCorrected.before: Read-only sounds like an easy approval path.
learnedAndCorrected.after: gmail.readonly and gmail.metadata are both restricted. Send-only is sensitive, and changes the product's capabilities.

learnedAndCorrected.before: Creating a client means the app is launch-ready.
learnedAndCorrected.after: The console form can be reached quickly while public restricted-data use still has verification and assessment gates.

learnedAndCorrected.before: Generic OAuth client instructions cover agents.
learnedAndCorrected.after: Live UI and current client help expose explicit AI-agent declaration and isolation guidance. This does not grant scopes or remove verification.

learnedAndCorrected.before: AI mail summaries are inherently disallowed.
learnedAndCorrected.after: Workspace policy lists generative summaries as an email-productivity use case, subject to Limited Use, disclosure and AI-data restrictions. A reviewer must assess the actual design.

uncertainties: No approval duration measured first-hand; timing is provider-published guidance.
Active effort ranges are planning estimates, not provider SLAs.
No security assessor price, remediation effort or current assessment tier verified.
Official credential guidance differs in phrasing about web client secrets; follow the confidential server client's current configuration and applicable runtime contract.
Provider rules can change; recheck sources before submitting.
